No field source places the tracker in a class of the archive's own (aggregators of machine-mediated reception work is the MMRS record's class, an archive source, ledgered as MMRS claims and not run as an O-class). The aliases are the entity's name, its short form 'AI Incident Tracker' (with 'AIRI', as MIT FutureTech's news writes it), its host, its operator's name and its pipeline's maker. The AI Incident Database and the MIT AI Risk Repository are distinct entities (derived_from, part_of) and are not aliases. Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on the tracker, or applies an archive category to incident trackers or to LLM classification of incident reports as a class; a bare mention, a link list or a generic use of 'classify' about another object is not a claim.
